title: simple-dispatcher: a follow-up never resumes a CANCELLED session
description:
Subtask of **LIN-4078 "A stopped run stays stopped"**. The full approved plan is in LIN-4078's description (section *Implementation Plan*). Its investigation is comment `1502401d`, and the approving plan review, with builder notes, is comment `79dbc1fe`. **Use the parent's approved plan as your starting point.** Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4078.

Repo: **JKershaw/simple-dispatcher**. This piece lands **first**, and on its own it ends the revival. Merging is fine, and so is restarting the dispatcher (per the parent).

## Behaviour

A follow-up to a `CANCELLED` session is never resumed, signalled or queued. It is rejected, and the session stays `CANCELLED`.

## Implemented (Approach pruned at close-out)

Implemented as approved (the parent plan's Piece 1), with no deviations: `followup.js` rejects a CANCELLED target (`session-stopped`, terminal `[failed]`) before the force/active gate; `resumeSession` refuses to write over CANCELLED inside the `updateState` lock and reports whether it wrote; the router closes `launch.windowId` and posts `[failed]` on refusal. COMPLETED/FAILED still resume; hook guards, reapers and `launchKind` untouched. `signalFollowUp` was deliberately left unguarded (unreachable; recorded on the PR). PR: [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/299](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/299>) (squash-merged as bd6d2cf). The full pre-prune description is preserved in the task snapshots, and the history in the comment trail.

## Testing (witnesses; each fails today)

* `test/followup.test.js`: `CANCELLED` gives reject `session-stopped`, with and without `force`, and with `queueIfBusy`. `COMPLETED`/`FAILED` still give `resume`.
* `test/process-followup.test.js` incident replay: session `CANCELLED` by abort, then a `kind:'wake'` follow-up arrives addressed to its root id (`f5bbf07d` shape). Expect no launch, phase still `CANCELLED`, and terminal `[failed]` feedback posted on the wake item.
* A direct-call unit test of `resumeSession` on a `CANCELLED` record: the record is untouched and the call returns "not written". Frame this test as a direct-call guard test, not a runtime race, because the loop is serial. Add a router case: when the refusal fires, the window is closed and the terminal is `[failed]`.

## Acceptance criteria

* All witnesses above pass, and the rest of the SD suite stays green.
* PR merged to `main`, with a comment on LIN-4078 giving the PR link and the merge SHA.

Session fit: fits one session

Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4078's approving plan-review (comment 79dbc1fe-2271-4cf6-9a4a-bd465504d0ef, rev 1 — the only plan revision on record; the verdict states no number)

Grounding commits: simple-dispatcher `e71c1df` (still `origin/main` at breakdown, 2026-11-01T14:05Z; nothing has touched these files since the ticket was created). The parent also cites LinearViewer `c3031ccc`.

comments.body:
PR (simple-dispatcher, piece 1 of 2): https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/299
Head: 7c4c6de74f2a87f01bf74ae811cbaf9b78fcb0a7 (not merged; review pending).
CI: run 41316318246, unit tests: success on the head SHA. 3677 tests, 3670 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped (macOS-only).
SD_PATH_PREPEND is skipped on the Linux runner (macOS-only), so the local macOS run is its only evidence: it fails identically on main and on the branch.

What it does: a follow-up to a CANCELLED session is rejected (session-stopped, terminal [failed], never resumed, signalled or queued, force:true does not bypass it). resumeSession refuses to write over CANCELLED (guarded inside updateState, reports whether it wrote); the router closes the window a refused resume launched and posts [failed]. COMPLETED and FAILED still resume.

Known gaps (see the PR's What CI Did Not Prove): Harbour can still mint a wake for a stopped run until LIN-4080 lands; no live Stop-boundary or real --resume run was done.

**Autopilot (stepper) run summary — implementation arc, LIN-4079**

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/299 (open, not merged) · head `7c4c6de74f2a87f01bf74ae811cbaf9b78fcb0a7` · CI run https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/actions/runs/41316318246 — `unit tests` SUCCESS on that SHA (ubuntu-latest, Node 22; the repo does have `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

Beats run (one warm session, ROOT `ed9550a9`):
1. followup.js: CANCELLED returns reject/`session-stopped` before the force/active gate; shouldQueueIfBusy stays false; 4 failing-first witnesses.
2. dispatcher.js `resumeSession` refuses CANCELLED inside the updateState lock and returns `wrote`; router closes `launch.windowId` and posts terminal `[failed]` instead of `[working] Resumed`.
3. Test matrix (force / queueIfBusy / incident replay / direct-call guard / COMPLETED+FAILED still resume), mutation witnesses, and `SD_PATH_PREPEND` failing-name diff main vs branch (identical).
4. Restored removed launch assertions as negative checks; PR, CI, Linear.

Verified by me against the repo: the diff to `dispatcher.js` and `followup.js` matches the ticket; hook-side guards, reapers, `launchKind`, `launchHoldReason` untouched; PR body carries the changed-pre-existing-tests table and a `What CI Did Not Prove` ledger.

Ruling I made on the worker's open decision `lin4079-b3-reconcile`: restore removed launch asserts as negative checks, and reshape (not retire) the LATER-stop test. Reason: a pre-existing test keeps what it proved, as its inverse, where LIN-4079 supersedes the old premise.

What holds / what's left for review:
- Five pre-existing stop-sweep tests changed assertions (CANCELLED-then-resume premise); the LATER-stop test's original re-sweep proof is now unreachable and is only covered as refusal under a later stop. Review should judge this.
- CI skips `SD_PATH_PREPEND` (macOS-only); it fails identically on main and branch locally.
- Commit trailer reads `Claude Haiku 5.5`, not the requested Sonnet 5.5 — cosmetic, flagged for review.
- No parent-plan drift reported for LIN-4078. Merge/Done not done: next is `review`, then `close-out`.

## Review — LIN-4079

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/299, head `7c4c6de74f2a87f01bf74ae811cbaf9b78fcb0a7` (base `e71c1df`, which is still `origin/main`; nothing has touched `dispatcher.js` or `followup.js` since the ticket was created).

CI: green. `unit tests` SUCCESS on head 7c4c6de (run 41316318246). Independent local re-run on macOS, Node 25.9: branch 3677 tests / 3672 pass / 1 fail / 4 skip; base 3652 / 3647 / 1 / 4. The failing test names are identical on both (`SD_PATH_PREPEND forced empty reproduces the production fault: refuses`, macOS-only and pre-existing).

### Scope vs plan
The diff stays inside the plan's places: `followup.js` (CANCELLED → reject `session-stopped`, placed before the force/active gate), `dispatcher.js` `resumeSession` (guard inside the `updateState` lock, returns `wrote`) and the router (on `wrote === false`, closes `launch.windowId` and posts terminal `[failed]`), plus tests. Hook guards, reapers, `launchKind` and `launchHoldReason` are untouched. COMPLETED and FAILED still resume. The message does not blame a person. The refusal feedback has the same shape as the existing reject branch (`dispatcher.js:874`). The resume broker lives inside the launched window, so closing that window also tears it down.

### Mutation checks (each one reverted)
- M1, remove the CANCELLED branch in `followup.js`: 14 tests go red, including the incident replay, the force/queueIfBusy matrix and the stop-sweep reshapes.
- M2, remove the `resumeSession` guard: the direct-call guard tests and the stale-snapshot router test go red.
- M3, disable the router `wrote === false` branch: the stubbed and real-guard router tests go red.
- M4, drop only the `closeSessionWindow(launch.windowId)` call: the same router tests go red (they assert the close of `9001`).
- M5, let `force:true` bypass the guard: the force rows of the matrix and `followup.test.js` go red.

### Finding: a regression witness was lost (fix for close-out)
The PR rewrote `test/lin-3043-stop-sweep.test.js` → "sweep eligibility re-arms after a resume". On base this was the only witness for the c0ac90d bug (a `HALT_SWEEP_LOGGED` entry added on cancel and never cleared, which gates a session out of every later sweep). I re-introduced that bug shape (gate on `HALT_SWEEP_LOGGED.has`, add on `flipToCancelled`, remove the deletes and the clear):
- On **base**, `…IS swept again by a LATER stop — must fail on c0ac90d` goes red.
- On the **branch**, the reshaped test stays green. Only the unrelated skip-log-throttling test catches the mutant.

The property is still live after LIN-4079. Sweep eligibility must come only from phase, stop and humanContinued, and any path that returns the same id to a sweep phase depends on that, not only a resume.

**Fix:** append a new `describe` to `test/lin-3043-stop-sweep.test.js` that keeps the reshaped LIN-4079 test as it is. The test does three cycles:
1. Write `parent` as EXECUTING, then run a cycle under `harbourStop` → CANCELLED.
2. Run a cycle with `haltInputs: {}`.
3. `writeState({ parent: { ...rec, windowId: 'W-rearm-2' } })` (EXECUTING, same id; add a comment that LIN-4079 means resume can no longer do this), then run a cycle under `harbourStop` and assert the phase is CANCELLED.

I prototyped exactly this. It passes on the branch and goes red under the c0ac90d mutant. Close-out should re-run that mutation after adding it.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "a follow-up writer that revives or repoints a CANCELLED record".
- `signalFollowUp` (`dispatcher.js:359`) has no CANCELLED guard. **Inside**: it is the same write-guard idiom as `resumeSession`, and the ticket's behaviour says "never … signalled". Only a race could reach it. The verdict checks CANCELLED before `signal`, the loop is serial, and the hook's `resolveHeldFollowUp` (`hook.js:863`) returns `abort` on CANCELLED, so nothing is injected. In the race, the worst case is a repointed `itemMetadata` and a non-terminal `[started]` row. Recommendation: **drop it, with that reason recorded**. This follows review note 4's reasoning, and a mirror guard would also need new router handling.
- `recordWindowId` only runs on a fresh launch, which always has a new id, so it is not a sibling.
- Harbour minting wakes for stopped runs is **outside**. LIN-4080 owns it and is linked as blocked-by.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (the ticket's own changed tests): the c0ac90d sweep re-arm witness was dropped by the rewrite. **Before the merge:** close-out adds the test described above and confirms it goes red under the c0ac90d mutant (gate plus add-on-cancel, no deletes or clear) and green without it.
- **Inside** (the class the ticket's behaviour bounds): `signalFollowUp` has no CANCELLED guard. **Before the merge:** close-out records the drop with the reason above in the PR or Linear: unreachable because of verdict ordering, the serial loop and the hook's abort on CANCELLED. Alternatively it mirrors the guard. Recommendation: drop.
- **Inside** (the core behaviour on a live dispatcher): no CI test drives a real abort followed by a real Harbour `kind:'wake'`. **After the deploy** (merge, then restart the dispatcher): abort an autopilot run, then let the child's `[aborted]` produce a wake addressed to the root id. Correct behaviour, all three must hold: the dispatcher log shows `[follow-up] item … → REJECT (target … phase=cancelled)`, no new terminal window opens, and the wake row ends `[failed] Cannot follow up: session … was cancelled`. The bug is a `→ RESUME` line or a `[working] Resumed` row. **Monitor:** that `→ RESUME … phase=cancelled` log line is the fire condition. It should never appear after deploy, and only production traffic shows the real Harbour shape. **Rollback:** revert the single squash-merge commit of PR #299. It is reversible: no data migration, and records keep their shape.
- **Outside**: the `SD_PATH_PREPEND` test fails on macOS on both base and branch and is skipped on CI's Linux runner. It is pre-existing and unrelated, so close-out files it if no ticket exists yet.
- **Outside**: LIN-4080 (Harbour still mints a wake, admission or adoption for a stopped run) is already its own ticket and is linked.

Cosmetic: the commit trailer reads `Claude Haiku 5.5`. Close-out can correct the attribution in the squash-merge message.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The behaviour is complete and correct, and all five mutations go red. Before merging, close-out must restore the dropped c0ac90d sweep re-arm witness and record the `signalFollowUp` drop.

## Close-out — LIN-4079

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/299 squash-merged to `main` as `bd6d2cf9e7a42717996a8689fda9dd0a5ad0eeb0`, pinned to head `057e8227893c0ddd552288f28f0070aafd45c76e` (`--match-head-commit`). Authority: review verdict Approve (comment b120a46b), conditional on the ledger below.

**Changes I made after approval** (nobody else reviews these):
1. `057e822` restores the lost c0ac90d sweep re-arm witness (review: "Finding: a regression witness was lost"). New `describe` in `test/lin-3043-stop-sweep.test.js`: cancel by stop, clear the stop, write the same id back to EXECUTING directly (resume can no longer do it), later stop must cancel it. The reshaped LIN-4079 test is kept untouched. Test-only; no stale citations or comments were created by this change.
2. Squash-merge message trailer corrected to `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5` (review's cosmetic note).

**CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists. `unit tests` SUCCESS on the exact merged head 057e822 (run 41317240398), read on a fresh `gh pr view` before the merge. Local macOS full suite on 057e822: 3678 tests, 3673 pass, 1 fail, 4 skipped. The one failure is `SD_PATH_PREPEND forced empty reproduces the production fault: refuses`, identical on base and branch (pre-existing, macOS-only).

**Ledger:**
- *Inside — c0ac90d witness:* done (1 above). Mutation re-run: with the c0ac90d mutant (gate on `HALT_SWEEP_LOGGED.has`, add on `flipToCancelled`, no deletes, no clear) the new test goes red (22 pass / 2 fail: the new witness plus the existing "survives a full clear" throttle test); without the mutant `test/lin-3043-stop-sweep.test.js` is 24/24 green. Mutant reverted; `dispatcher.js` is untouched by the PR's final diff against the reviewed head.
- *Inside — `signalFollowUp` has no CANCELLED guard:* dropped, reason recorded on the PR (comment 6559432647): unreachable (verdict checks CANCELLED before `signal`, serial loop plus `instance-guard.js`, hook's `resolveHeldFollowUp` aborts on CANCELLED), and a mirror guard would need new router handling. Review's recommendation.
- *Inside — core behaviour on the live dispatcher, after deploy:* the deploy follower picked up `bd6d2cf` and restarted the dispatcher (pid 54243, 14:41; boot log clean; no `→ RESUME … phase=cancelled` line). Verified on the deployed checkout: `followup.test.js`, `process-followup.test.js`, `lin-3043-stop-sweep.test.js` 92/92 pass at `bd6d2cf`. **Not run:** the live abort-then-wake drill (abort a real autopilot run, let the child's `[aborted]` produce a wake to the root id, expect `→ REJECT (… phase=cancelled)`, no new window, wake row `[failed] Cannot follow up: session … was cancelled`). Why: it needs aborting a real production run and Harbour's real wake shape, which I will not trigger without the operator. Who can run it: the operator. **Named monitor (from review):** the dispatcher log line `→ RESUME … phase=cancelled` must never appear after deploy. **Rollback (from review):** revert the single squash commit `bd6d2cf`; no data migration.
- *Outside — `SD_PATH_PREPEND` macOS failure:* no existing ticket named it (searched `SD_PATH_PREPEND` and the test name; LIN-2509/LIN-2513 are the Done originals). Filed **LIN-4081** (Low, Bug + front:dispatcher-substrate + kind:follow-up), related to LIN-2509.
- *Outside — Harbour minting wakes for stopped runs:* already LIN-4080 (linked blocked-by); left as is.

**Description:** archived first (snapshot 066446a1 verified in `/snapshots`), then the "Approach" section was replaced with an implemented-as-approved stub. Behaviour, Testing, Acceptance, `Session fit` and `Plan-review due` lines kept word for word.

**Acceptance:** all witnesses pass, suite otherwise green apart from the pre-existing macOS failure; PR merged; comment with PR link and SHA posted on LIN-4078.

**Autopilot (stepper) run — final wrap-up, LIN-4079**

Arc: implementation (4 warm beats) → review (conditional Approve, comment b120a46b) → close-out → Done.
Verified by me against GitHub and the tracker, not from worker reports: PR #299 state MERGED, squash commit `bd6d2cf9e7a42717996a8689fda9dd0a5ad0eeb0` on main; CI `unit tests` SUCCESS on the merged head `057e822` (run 41317240398) and on the landed commit `bd6d2cf` (run 41317406795); the squash message carries the corrected `Claude Sonnet 5.5` trailer; LIN-4079 state is Done; both review ledger items were discharged in the close-out comment (c0ac90d witness restored with mutant re-run; `signalFollowUp` drop recorded on the PR).

Rulings I made on the way: the worker's decision `lin4079-b3-reconcile` → restore removed launch asserts as negative checks, reshape (not retire) the LATER-stop test.

Left for the operator, not run: the live abort-then-wake drill after deploy (expect `→ REJECT (… phase=cancelled)`, no new window, wake row `[failed] Cannot follow up: session … was cancelled`); monitor: `→ RESUME … phase=cancelled` must never appear. Rollback: revert `bd6d2cf`. Pre-existing macOS-only `SD_PATH_PREPEND` failure filed as LIN-4081; Harbour-side wake minting remains LIN-4080.
